mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate is below 5% signals supply-side disruptions in an otherwise healthy labor market, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate higher prices and profit margins.
regime_hint: supply shock in tight labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS growth > 5% for three consecutive months) without a corresponding rise in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1 flat) signals pent-up household savings that could translate into future demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 5% for 3 consecutive months AND GDPC1 flat (change < 0.2%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the CPIAUCSL index of more than 1% month-over-month signals a sharp disinflation or deflation shock, which historically has been associated with increased uncertainty and negative risk sentiment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate simultaneously falls below 4% signals an overheating labor market, which historically precedes monetary tightening and higher input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% for four consecutive months signals a robust residential construction cycle, which is historically associated with higher demand for materials and capital goods, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of periods where the trigger is active.
